title: Satan in Despair, but Hope in Small Deeds • Debts, Trusts, Bequests • Today I Have Perfected • At ‘Arafah with Raised Hands • After Sunset, Slowly • Al-Fadl’s Eyes • Pebbles and a Hundred Camels at Mina • On Behalf of the People of the House Too • The Share of Hair • The Address on the Day of Sacrifice • Beside Zamzam

blocks.0: Satan in Despair, but Hope in Small Deeds
blocks.1: Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) has related another part of the Farewell Hajj address. The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.2: Satan has despaired of being worshipped in this land of yours. But he is pleased if he is obeyed in other things, which you regard as trivial. So beware.{{1}}
blocks.3: That this open idol-worship will not go on in the land of Arabia is Satan’s last hope. His reliance now is on those small deeds which we do not take notice of. A slight lie, a slight word, a slight negligence. Then in that same narration came the matter of the path and the matter of the brother,
blocks.4: O people, I am leaving among you something which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet. Every Muslim is a brother of another Muslim; Muslims are brothers. It is not lawful for anyone to take his brother’s wealth unless he gives it from the pleasure of his heart. Do not wrong. And do not become disbelievers after me, cutting one another’s necks.{{1}}
blocks.5: Beside the Qur’an he also mentioned his own Sunnah. Book and Sunnah, both must be held. Hold one and leave the other, and in the hand remains half the path. And the brother’s right. A brother’s wealth cannot be taken beyond the pleasure of his heart.
blocks.7: The Farewell Hajj address had mention of debt and trust too. Abu Umamah al-Bahili (RA) had heard that address. He says,
blocks.8: I heard the Messenger of Allah {{1}} say in the address in the year of the Farewell Hajj: Allah has given every rightful person his right. So there is no bequest for an heir.{{2}}
blocks.9: And the next sentences are about debt,
blocks.10: What is borrowed must be returned. An animal taken for milk must be returned. A debt must be paid. And the guarantor is responsible.{{1}}
blocks.11: In the Farewell Hajj address, before that vast gathering, it is being said, a debt must be paid, a loan must be returned. There could be no greater stage for speaking of debt and trust. And in five acts the path to Paradise. In another narration of Abu Umamah (RA),
blocks.12: Fear Allah your Lord. Pray your five prayers. Fast your month. Give zakah on your wealth. Obey those in charge of your affairs. You will enter the Paradise of your Lord.{{1}}
blocks.13: By the measure of an address it is one sentence. But the whole design of a life is here: fear, prayer, fasting, zakah, obedience. At the start taqwa, at the end Paradise. To whom is the matter of debt being said? To the countless listeners of that day, and through them to me. The debt that is on my neck today, I know its name.
blocks.15: That afternoon at ‘Arafah. The address finished. Bilal (RA) gave the adhan, then the iqamah; Zuhr. Again the iqamah; ‘Asr. No other prayer between the two prayers. Then the Prophet {{1}} stood, with the belly of the she-camel toward the rocks, facing the qiblah, until sunset. On this day of ‘Arafah a verse of the Qur’an was revealed, of which even the Jews later spoke to ‘Umar (RA).{{2}}
blocks.18: Today the disbelievers have despaired of (overcoming) your religion. So do not fear them. Place the fear of Me in your hearts. Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam for you as your religion (for all time).{{1}}
blocks.19: The Jewish man had said to ‘Umar (RA),
blocks.20: Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your Book that you recite. Had it been revealed upon us Jews, we would have made that day an ‘Eid. ‘Umar said, which verse? He said, ‘Today I have perfected your religion for you…’. ‘Umar said, we know that day and that place where this was revealed to the Prophet {{1}}. He was then standing at ‘Arafah, on the day of Jumu‘ah.{{2}}
blocks.21: A Jewish man had said the same to Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) too. He answered,
blocks.22: It was revealed on two ‘Eid days: the day of Jumu‘ah and the day of ‘Arafah.{{1}}
blocks.23: That day two ‘Eids came together. The ‘Eid of Jumu‘ah, and the ‘Eid of ‘Arafah. And on that day Allah said, the religion is complete. Hearing the verse ‘Umar (RA) wept. The Prophet {{1}} asked, why do you weep? He said, after completion, nothing at all remains but incompleteness. The Prophet {{2}} said, you have spoken the truth.{{3}}
blocks.24: The religion is complete. This means, before me now are two paths: to follow what is there, or, speaking of following, to create something new. In the religion Allah Himself has declared complete there is no place for my addition. My place is only in practising. And the reason for ‘Umar’s weeping he himself has stated: after completion only deficiency remains. The one way to stop that deficiency: to hold fast to what has been completed.
blocks.26: The hour before sunset. The Prophet {{1}} on the she-camel, facing the qiblah. Seated behind him Usamah ibn Zayd (RA). He says,
blocks.27: I was sitting behind the Prophet {{1}} at ‘Arafat. He raised both hands and supplicated. His she-camel tilted to one side, and the rein fell. He picked up the rein with one hand, and kept the other hand raised.{{2}}
blocks.28: The hand did not stop. The she-camel tilted, the rein fell, one hand came down for the rein. The other hand still toward Allah. For how long do our hands rise for supplication? At one sound they come down.
blocks.29: And what is that day like? ‘A’ishah (RA) has narrated from the Prophet {{1}},
blocks.30: On no day does Allah free more servants from Hell than on the day of ‘Arafah. He draws near, then boasts of them before the angels, saying, what do these want?{{1}}
blocks.31: The day on which the Prophet {{1}} stood with raised hands is the very day of the most freedom from Hell. And on that very day he spoke of women’s rights and of the paying of debts. What do these want? Before this question of Allah I too stand, whenever I raise my hands. Today what do I ask of Allah?
blocks.33: The sun set. From the plain of ‘Arafah a stream of people toward Muzdalifah. The Prophet {{1}} seated Usamah (RA) behind himself. He pulled the she-camel’s rein so tightly, Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.34: He held the rein of al-Qaswa so tightly that her head was touching his saddle. And with his right hand he was saying, O people, calmly, calmly.{{1}}
blocks.35: Everyone is rushing, everyone wants to arrive quickly. And he, holding the rein tight, is saying, slowly. The she-camel’s head touches the saddle, so hard the rein. Because where the crowd is bigger, the harm of haste is greater.
blocks.36: Reaching Muzdalifah, Maghrib and ‘Isha’ with one adhan and two iqamahs. No nafl between the two prayers. Then Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.37: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} lay down, until Fajr.{{2}}
blocks.38: The address of the whole day, the supplication, the standing. The next morning pebbles, sacrifice, many tasks. This night in between he spent sleeping. The Sunnah is not only of standing, but also of sleeping. He who knows when resting will make the morning’s work come right. And as the light of Fajr appeared, at al-Mash‘ar al-Haram. Facing the qiblah, supplication, takbir, tahlil. Until the sky had grown quite bright.
blocks.40: Departure from Muzdalifah before sunrise. This time behind the Prophet’s {{1}} she-camel sat al-Fadl ibn ‘Abbas (RA). Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.41: Al-Fadl was a man of fine hair, fair, handsome. When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} set off, a group of women passed beside him. Al-Fadl began to look at them. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} placed his hand on al-Fadl’s face. Al-Fadl turned his face and began to look the other way. Then the Messenger of Allah {{3}} brought his hand from the other side and again placed it on al-Fadl’s face, so that he would turn away.{{4}}
blocks.42: No scolding. No reprimand. One hand, on the face. Al-Fadl turned, the Prophet’s {{1}} hand turned too. Al-Fadl’s eyes turned to the other side. A correction that shames no one. Without speaking, the word gets across. In our homes, mosques, madrasahs, when catching someone’s error of the eyes we often raise our voice. The mistake that could have been settled with one hand, we call out before people.
blocks.43: Pebbles and a Hundred Camels at Mina
blocks.44: Reaching Mina, the first act: seven pebbles at the big Jamrah. Jabir (RA) saw the Prophet {{1}} throwing pebbles sitting on his camel. And saying,
blocks.45: Take your rites of Hajj from me. For I do not know whether I will be able to perform Hajj again after this Hajj.{{1}}
blocks.46: He himself is saying, this may be the last Hajj. So what is to be learned, learn it today. After this statement every act of Hajj is no longer just an act, it becomes an inheritance.
blocks.47: After the pebbles, the sacrifice. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.48: He sacrificed sixty-three (camels) with his own hand. Then he gave to ‘Ali; ‘Ali sacrificed the rest, and he made ‘Ali a partner in his sacrifice. Then he commanded that a piece of meat from each camel be taken and cooked in one pot. The two of them ate that meat and drank the broth.{{1}}
blocks.49: First with his own hand. Then ‘Ali. And taking ‘Ali as a partner in his sacrifice. A piece each from a hundred camels in one pot. On the greatest day of celebration he and ‘Ali together tasted the same pot.
blocks.50: On Behalf of the People of the House Too
blocks.51: The reckoning of a hundred camels, and the bustle of the crowd. Yet the people of the house were not forgotten. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.52: On the day of sacrifice beef was brought to us. I said, what is this? It was said, the Messenger of Allah {{1}} has sacrificed on behalf of his wives.{{2}}
blocks.53: Sixty-three camels by his own hand, a hundred in all, and the leadership of a vast gathering. Yet even in the piece of meat that came to the house, the names of the wives. One who is a great person, though he has a thousand tasks outside, does not forget the share of the people of his house.
blocks.55: After finishing the sacrifice the Prophet {{1}} called the barber. Anas ibn Malik (RA) says,
blocks.56: He said to the barber, take. And he gestured toward the right side, then the left. Then he began giving that hair to the people.{{1}}
blocks.58: He began with the right side, and distributed that hair among the people, a strand or two at a time. Then he said the left side, the barber did that too. Then he said, Abu Talhah is here. And he gave it to Abu Talhah.{{1}}
blocks.59: He distributed with his own hand, one or two at a time, into the hands of those who were near. For those into whose hands that hair fell that day, it was the memory of the Beloved. For us today, the way to repay that debt of love is to walk the path he taught.
blocks.60: The Address on the Day of Sacrifice
blocks.61: The morning of the day of sacrifice wore on. Another address at Mina. Rafi‘ ibn ‘Amr al-Muzani (RA) says,
blocks.62: I saw the Messenger of Allah {{1}} at Mina, when the sun had risen well (in the forenoon), addressing the people, seated on a grey-white mule. ‘Ali was explaining on his behalf (conveying his words). Some of the people standing, some sitting.{{2}}
blocks.63: Even on that morning at Mina there were many people, some standing, some sitting. Where the voice did not reach, there was ‘Ali’s (RA) voice. That address at Mina began with a question. Abu Bakrah (RA) says, the Prophet {{1}} addressed us on the day of sacrifice,
blocks.64: He asked, do you know what day this is? We said, Allah and His Messenger know best. He remained silent; we thought he would perhaps give it another name. He said, is it not the day of sacrifice? We said, indeed. He asked, what month is this? We said, Allah and His Messenger know best. He remained silent; we thought he would perhaps give another name. He said, is it not Dhu al-Hijjah? We said, indeed. He asked, what city is this? We said, Allah and His Messenger know best. He remained silent; we thought he would perhaps give another name. He said, is it not the sacred city? We said, indeed.{{1}}
blocks.65: Three questions, three silences. Each time the Companions thought, some new name is coming. Yet he made them hold to the familiar name: the day of sacrifice, Dhu al-Hijjah, Makkah. By the style of such a question and answer he led people to the right place, where the sanctity of this day, this month, this city lodges in everyone’s mind. Then with that sanctity he measured the sanctity of a Muslim’s blood. And at the end Abu Bakrah (RA) says,
blocks.66: He said, have I conveyed? They said, yes. He said, O Allah, be witness. Let those who are present convey to those who are absent. For often the one to whom it is conveyed understands better than the listener. And do not become disbelievers after me, cutting one another’s necks.{{1}}
blocks.67: Making Allah witness, and with it a warning. That after him Muslims should not raise a hand against one another’s necks. And he placed the responsibility on every listener: whoever hears will convey. Of what we learn, how much do we convey to anyone? Hoarded knowledge was not the Prophet’s {{1}} wish.
blocks.69: The sacrifice and the hair done. Then returning to the Ka‘bah for tawaf, and Zuhr in Makkah. Then Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.70: Then he came to Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib, who were giving the pilgrims water to drink beside Zamzam. He said, Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib, draw water. Were it not that people would push you aside from your work of serving water, I would draw water with you myself. They handed him a bucket, and he drank from it.{{1}}
blocks.71: The duty of drawing water from the well of Zamzam belongs to his clan. Honour by lineage. That honoured work he himself wished to do, yet did not. Why? If people see him drawing water himself, everyone will rush to join him. In the crowd the clan’s honoured work itself will be covered. From the work in which a leader’s touching would narrow the place of others, he kept away. To suppress one’s own eagerness to protect another’s right.

footnotes.0: Al-Mustadrak, al-Hakim 318, from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), through ‘Ikrimah. Ruling: Ibn al-Mulaqqin ‘jayyid’; Ibn Hazm, al-Ihkam 2/251: ‘sahih’; al-Mundhiri, al-Targhib wa-al-Tarhib 1/61: the chain ‘sahih or hasan or close to it’; al-Albani, Sahih al-Targhib 40: ‘sahih’. The narration explicitly mentions that it was the Farewell Hajj address.
footnotes.1: Al-Mustadrak, al-Hakim 318 (the same narration; the ruling above applies). Another route for holding fast to ‘the Book of Allah and the Sunnah’: Muwatta’ Malik (as a balagh); Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr, al-Tamhid 24/331: ‘mahfuz, ma‘ruf, mashhur’; al-Albani, Hidayat al-Ruwat 184: the chain ‘hasan’. The narration on the Book of Allah in ‘Sahih Muslim 1218’ is in the earlier part.
footnotes.2: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 2120 (from Abu Umamah al-Bahili (RA); said to be ‘hasan’ or ‘hasan sahih’). The same hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud 3565 and 2870; where Isma‘il ibn ‘Ayyash narrates from the Syrians, a large group of scholars have held his narration acceptable (Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari 5/438: this narration is through Shurahbil ibn Muslim, who is Syrian and thiqah); Ibn al-Qattan, al-Wahm wa-al-Iham 4/189 and Ibn al-Mulaqqin, al-Badr al-Munir 7/263: ‘hasan’; al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 2210: ‘sahih’.
footnotes.3: Sunan Abi Dawud 3565 (from Abu Umamah al-Bahili (RA); the ruling in the note above applies). ‘Al-minhah’ = a camel or goat given temporarily for drinking its milk. These sentences are in Abu Dawud without mention of the Farewell Hajj, of the same chain as the Farewell Hajj narration of al-Tirmidhi (2120).
footnotes.4: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 616 (from Abu Umamah al-Bahili (RA); al-Tirmidhi: ‘hasan sahih’; al-Albani, Sahih al-Tirmidhi 616 and al-Silsilah al-Sahihah 867: ‘sahih’). ‘Dha amrikum’ = those in charge of your affairs (rulers and leaders). The narration explicitly says ‘the Farewell Hajj address’.
footnotes.5: The adhan, two iqamahs, Zuhr and ‘Asr together, no other prayer between: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Time of the verse’s revelation: Sahih al-Bukhari 45, Sahih Muslim 3017 (from ‘Umar (RA); on the day of ‘Arafah). In the sirah account (al-Rahiq al-Makhtum, Bengali, pp. 751–752) revelation comes just as the address ended; in the sahih hadith the words ‘after the address’ are not there, so the narration says ‘on the day of ‘Arafah’.
footnotes.6: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, Surah al-Ma’idah 5:3, p. 303 (matched by rendering the printed page and reading). Note 7 (p. 303): ‘In various sahih hadiths it is that this verse was revealed at the time of the Farewell Hajj.’ Arabic: Al-Qur’an Cloud (Uthmani script). The earlier part of the verse (the list of forbidden foods) is omitted here.
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari 45 (from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA), through Tariq ibn Shihab; sahih). Also in Sahih Muslim 3017 (where Sufyan has said he has doubt whether it was Friday).
footnotes.8: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3044 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), through ‘Ammar ibn Abi ‘Ammar). Al-Albani, Hidayat al-Ruwat 1317: ‘sahih’; Ibn Hajar (Hidayat al-Ruwat 2/97): it has a shahid in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim (the hadith of ‘Umar).
footnotes.9: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 752 (source: Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari; note 736). Disagreement over the chain: Shu‘ayb Arna’ut, Takhrij al-Musnad 20528: ‘the chain is weak’ (an unknown narrator); in Arna’ut 25/101 another route ‘weak and mursal’; Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah 5/189: one route ‘jayyid’; Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari 8/120: ‘weak’. In a sahih chain this weeping is not mentioned. So it has come only as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.10: Sunan al-Nasa’i 3011 (from Usamah ibn Zayd (RA), through ‘Ata’); al-Albani, Sahih al-Nasa’i 3011: ‘the chain is sahih’; Arna’ut, Takhrij al-Musnad 21821: ‘sahih’; Ibn Hajar, Fath al-Bari 11/147: ‘the chain is jayyid’. Usamah (RA) sat behind him from ‘Arafah to Muzdalifah (Sahih Muslim 1218).
footnotes.11: Sahih Muslim 1348 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); sahih); al-Hakim 1726 (‘sahih al-isnad’); Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr, al-Istidhkar 2/43: ‘sahih’. ‘Yadnu’ = draws near (befitting Allah’s majesty, in the general principle of Ahl al-Sunnah, without imagining a manner). The narration about the best supplication on the day of ‘Arafah (Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3585) has not been brought here because of weakness in the chain; verification sheet §6.
footnotes.12: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). ‘Al-sakinah’ = tranquillity, calm movement. Seating Usamah (RA) behind him is in the same narration too.
footnotes.13: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Maghrib and ‘Isha’ together, one adhan and two iqamahs, no nafl between: in the same narration. After the Fajr prayer, at al-Mash‘ar al-Haram facing the qiblah, supplication, takbir, tahlil and proclamation of tawhid, until the sky was clear: in the same narration.
footnotes.14: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Another form of this incident: the question of a woman of the Khath‘am tribe and al-Fadl’s looking (Sahih al-Bukhari 1513, from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); here only the narration of Muslim 1218.
footnotes.15: Sahih Muslim 1297 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Sunan al-Nasa’i 3062 (al-Albani, Sahih al-Nasa’i: sahih); Sunan Abi Dawud 1970; al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami‘ 5061: sahih. The wording is slightly different: ‘li-ta’khudhu manasikakum’ (so that you take your rites of Hajj).
footnotes.16: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the same narration: the sacrificial animals in all were one hundred (counting those brought by the Prophet {{1}} and ‘Ali (RA)). Sixty-three + thirty-seven = one hundred: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 753 (sirah-based; the number agrees with the narration of Muslim).
footnotes.17: Sahih al-Bukhari 1709 (from ‘A’ishah (RA), through ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, via Malik and Yahya ibn Sa‘id; sahih). ‘‘An azwajihi’ = on behalf of his wives. In the same narration, the command on the day of sacrifice to undo their ihram. (This part about beef is in some other routes too; here the route of al-Bukhari is taken.)
footnotes.18: Sahih Muslim 1305 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA); sahih). Ibn Hibban 3879: sahih; Arna’ut: the chain is sahih on the condition of Muslim.
footnotes.19: Sahih Muslim 1305 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA), the narration of Abu Kurayb; sahih). In another narration of the same chapter (Muslim 1305, the narration of Abu Bakr) there is mention of giving the left-side hair to Umm Sulaym (RA).
footnotes.20: Sunan Abi Dawud 1956 (from Rafi‘ ibn ‘Amr al-Muzani (RA)). Al-Albani, Hidayat al-Ruwat 2604: ‘the chain is sahih’; ‘Abd al-Haqq al-Ishbili: sahih al-isnad. (In another route from ‘Amir al-Muzani, Arna’ut 15921: ‘weak’; here the route of Rafi‘ is taken.) Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 753 (the same account; source: Abu Dawud).
footnotes.21: Sahih al-Bukhari 1741 (from Abu Bakrah (RA); sahih). In the same narration, after this: ‘fa-inna dima’akum wa-amwalakum ‘alaykum haramun…’ (your blood and your wealth are sacred to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, this month, this city), which came in Dars 2. Sahih al-Bukhari 67 also has an account of the same style (of two questions).
footnotes.22: Sahih al-Bukhari 1741 (from Abu Bakrah (RA); sahih). ‘Fa-rubba mubalaghin aw‘a min sami‘’ (often the one to whom it is conveyed understands better than the listener). Sahih al-Bukhari 121 (from Jarir (RA)): ‘In the Farewell Hajj the Prophet {{1}} said to me, make the people silent; then he said: do not become disbelievers after me, cutting one another’s necks.’
footnotes.23: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami‘ 1494, 7899: sahih. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 753 (the same account). ‘Siqayah’ = the duty of giving the pilgrims water, which was the hereditary honour of Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib.

quiz.q: In al-Hakim’s narration, of what did the Prophet ﷺ say Satan had despaired?
o: Tawhid will endure
Muslims will gather in one row, in that hope
The Qur’an will remain preserved
He will be worshipped in the land of Arabia

quiz.q: What does the hadith ‘Satan is pleased with small deeds’ remind us?
o: Even a trivial slight lie or negligence can be obedience to Satan
Satan can no longer harm us at all, because he has despaired
Avoiding only major sins is enough
Small deeds should not be done at all

quiz.q: In the narration of al-Tirmidhi 2120, what did the Prophet ﷺ say in the Farewell Hajj address about the heir?
o: There is no bequest for an heir
An heir’s share can be reduced
A bequest may go up to half of the wealth
All heirs get equally

quiz.q: In another narration of Abu Umamah (RA), how many acts on the path to Paradise were mentioned?
o: Twelve
Five
Three
Four
quiz.e: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 616 (taqwa, prayer, fasting, zakah, obedience to those in charge).

quiz.q: By bringing in debt and trust in the address, which principle did the Prophet ﷺ make clear?
o: Keeping trusts is improper
Debts are paid only by the government
Returning loans, paying debts and fulfilling trusts carry accountability
Forgiving debt is the only and compulsory solution

quiz.q: Someone borrowed and for several months is not returning. What does the Farewell Hajj address say here?
o: A loan must be returned, a debt must be paid
Asking forgiveness of the loan is the Sunnah
Interceding for the debtor is enough
If there is no time, no harm

quiz.q: On which day, in ‘Umar (RA)’s narration, was the verse ‘Today I have perfected your religion’ revealed?
o: On the day of ‘Arafah, a Friday
On the day of sacrifice, in the field of Mina
On the day of the conquest of Makkah
On the middle day of Tashriq

quiz.q: What came in the sirah narration as the reason for ‘Umar (RA)’s weeping?
o: Because Hajj was coming to an end
After completion nothing remains but incompleteness
Because he remembered relatives
He wept in grief that one day the Prophet ﷺ would have to be bid farewell
quiz.e: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum, p. 752 (sirah-based; disagreement over the chain in the note).

quiz.q: Pulling the she-camel’s rein on the way to Muzdalifah, what was the Prophet ﷺ telling the people?
o: Faster, faster
Pick up pebbles
Calmly, calmly
Form rows

quiz.q: At Muzdalifah, after Maghrib and ‘Isha’, what did the Prophet ﷺ do until Fajr?
o: Stood in tahajjud
Lay down
Recited the Qur’an
Spent the night supplicating

quiz.q: What kind of correction does the incident of placing a hand on al-Fadl’s face teach?
o: Removing from the group
Stopping publicly with a rebuke before everyone
Giving punishment
Gently turning the face away without words

quiz.q: A friend’s error is being rebuked before everyone. From the incident of al-Fadl, which path can be learned?
o: Staying silent while seeing the error
Having others say it
Correcting softly and privately even without words
Giving harsh punishment before everyone for the error

quiz.q: How many camels did the Prophet ﷺ sacrifice with his own hand?
o: Sixty-three
Sixty
Thirty-seven
One hundred

quiz.q: At the throwing of pebbles, what does ‘take your rites of Hajj from me’ indicate?
o: These are the rules of an ordinary journey
It could be a last chance to learn
This is an old custom of the Arabs
This is a separate rule only for new pilgrims

quiz.q: Someone knows knowledge but shares it with no one. What does the address of the day of sacrifice remind them?
o: Showing off knowledge before everyone to raise one’s standing
Whoever has heard should convey it to others
Hoarding knowledge is better
Knowledge is only for scholars

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ refrain from drawing water at Zamzam himself?
o: The crowd might take away the siqayah work of Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib
There was no water in the well then
He was unable to draw water and the Companions were helping him
He was in ihram

quiz.q: Someone wants to do an honoured work himself, but it would narrow the place of another’s responsibility. What does the incident of Zamzam teach?
o: Suppressing one’s own eagerness to protect another’s right
